title_original: Art Lovers Movie Club: Nina Davies, ‘Precursing’, 2023￼
excerpt_original: The artist’s fictional video-podcast follows an imagined court case concerning a pedestrian killed by a self-driving car

blocks.text: The artist’s fictional video-podcast follows an imagined court case concerning a pedestrian killed by a self-driving car

The artist Nina Davies’s 2023 film is an uncanny exploration of the entanglements between technology and human behaviours. Uncanny, that is, because of the eerie plausibility of its near-future scenario. Precursing unfolds as a fictional video-podcast where the two hosts – Riley and Devon – discuss ‘Piasecki v. Wade’: an imagined court case concerning a pedestrian (Wade) killed by a self-driving car (Piasecki). Their conversation flows naturally, jumping from straightforward discussions about the case to adjacent anecdotes that paint a broader picture of what it means for autonomous predictive technologies to be let loose in society.

The hosts discuss ‘precursing’, a trend where people behave like NPCs (a videogame acronym for ‘non-player characters’), while playing social media clips of people precursing and shots of performers, sometimes rendered as CGI videogame characters, also strutting around like NPCs. The hosts explain how self-driving cars are trained in videogame environments , and thus are more likely to recognise people who are precursing. The rehearsed, predictable movement, therefore, became widely adopted as a sort of language to interact with self-driving vehicles. Wade was hit by a Piasecki car that didn’t correctly anticipate his movement – that is, ‘normal’ movement.

At the core of the discussion lies a debate around truth – and how society is structured around what people believe to be true. This is nothing new, as Davies acknowledges. Her research notes for Precursing include a 1804 British legal case involving a perpetrator and his genuine belief in ghosts. Today, we know that our lives are choreographed by algorithms and that the lines between the real and the artificial are blurry everywhere. In this shifting reality, Davis’s film asks, which new rules will we choose?
Art Lovers Movie Club: Nina Davies, Precursing , 2023, single channel HD video, 11 min. © the artist 17 November – 18 December 2026

Nina Davies is a Canadian-British artist who considers the present moment through observing how dance in popular culture is disseminated, circulated, made and consumed. Beginning with academic research and legal analysis, her work has evolved to incorporate fiction as a critical method by reimagining emerging dances of today as traditional practices of the future, and placing movement within larger socio-technical contexts. Through this, her practice builds frameworks for engaging with dance as something that acts on and within the world. Her work has been shown at Galerie Rudolfinum, Henry Moore Institute, FACT, Tate Britain, Somerset House and The Photographers Gallery. In 2021, she co-founded Future Artefacts FM, an artist-run program that showcases artists working with speculative fiction for broadcast which she co-hosts with artist Niamh Schmidtke and curator Rebecca Edwards.
